Anna — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed action items so we’re aligned before the POC kickoff.

Summary of what we captured on the call:
- Goal: validate end-to-end (client -> model -> client) p95/p99 latency for the Orion triage flow (avg payload ~450 tokens, 512 max) and confirm streaming chunk behavior for incremental responses.
- Orion targets: p95 <= 180 ms, p99 <= 450 ms (E2E) for normal working set.
- Incumbent baseline (from your slides): p95 ~ 320 ms, p99 ~ 1.2 s under production ingress.
- Throughput/scale: starting target 100 QPS sustained, expected bursts up to 250 QPS. Concurrency per worker: ~8 sessions.
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming with chunk flush <= 50 ms latency ideal; must support partial output for UI.

Action items (proposed):
1) Orion to share a small anonymized request set (50–200 representative prompts) and a sample client-side replay harness (or we’ll provide one).
2) Redwood to run lab runs against our hosted API with the same bot/model config and return p95/p99 + token latency distributions, plus a streaming trace.
3) Joint E2E test window (production-path network): schedule a 2-hour joint run where Orion routes traffic through a staging vanity endpoint so we measure e2e latency under realistic network conditions.
4) Deliverable: latency matrix (p50/p90/p95/p99), max sustainable QPS at target SLO, and streaming chunk latency report.

I’ve attached a starter latency matrix and an SLO proposal (see attachments). Proposed dates:
- Share dataset: by Thu 19 Nov
- Lab runs (Redwood): week of 23 Nov
- Joint E2E test: Wed 25 Nov (flexible)

Can you confirm those dates or propose alternatives? Also flag any additional constraints (data residency, IP allowlists, or procurement contacts).

Thanks,

Looping in a few engineering notes so the POC has the right measurement plan. High level: we need to separate model compute latency from e2e network/client latency and report both. Suggested methodology below.

Measurement plan (engineer-level):
- Lab runs (model-only): synthetic replay against a colocated client in our staging region to measure model-side p50/p90/p95/p99 and per-token generation time. Use fixed batch sizes (1, 4, 8) to show batching impact.
- E2E runs (client-observed): run the replay harness from Orion’s network (or from a client that simulates Orion NAT/IPs) to include TLS, proxy, and client queueing. Run multiple windows: steady-state (100 QPS), burst (250 QPS for 5 minutes), ramp test.
- Streaming checks: measure first-byte latency, average token flush latency, and chunk jitter for 1–8 token flushes. Redwood will run streaming with max chunk size of 4 tokens by default unless Orion prefers different chunking.

Preliminary lab numbers (informal, single shard, internal harness):
- Config: model-medium@fp16, sequence=512, batch=4, sim qps=80, concurrency=6
- Observed model-only: p95 = 150 ms, p99 = 420 ms, median token latency ~12 ms/token
- Sustained QPS @ p95 target 180 ms: single shard handled ~140 QPS before p95 drifted beyond 180 ms (no KV cache). With KV prefix caching (warm cache) we see effective p95 ~ 130 ms.

Notes and risks:
- The model-only runs do not include client TLS and network; expect E2E numbers to increase by ~30–60 ms depending on customer network paths and proxies.
- Incumbent’s higher p99 suggests tail behavior under their production topology; we should instrument percentiles across request sizes and user agents to compare apples-to-apples.
- For the joint E2E test, please provide a small set of real-client NAT IPs or proxy endpoints so we can run the replay from a path that mirrors production.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for the lab vs e2e measurements and share before the scheduled run.

—Vivek
